speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a pediatric patient with a low-grade fever, itchy rash, and joint pain after taking antibiotics. To understand what happened, did you take any specific type of antibiotic, and do you remember exactly when the symptoms started?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Amoxicillin-induced serum sickness-like reaction.

The rash starting in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading, combined with fever and joint pain one week after starting amoxicillin, is highly characteristic of this condition. Do you have a history of asthma, allergic rhinitis, or atopy, which increases the risk for this reaction?
